title: Second ghost menu bar icon on macOS Sonoma
body: After upgrading to macOS Sonoma 14.4.1, my Tauri menu bar app sporadically shows a strange second icon near the Apple icon. It only happens when an external monitor is connected with mirroring enabled. I can reproduce it with a generated Tauri system-tray app in either development mode or an installed DMG. I expect only the normal tray icon.

symptoms_visible: My Tauri menu bar app sporadically shows a second icon near the Apple icon on macOS Sonoma 14.4.1 when I use a mirrored external monitor.
N0.label: N0 ghost menu icon reported

symptoms_visible: The extra icon appeared when I had two virtual desktops, but disappeared as soon as I switched to another desktop and did not return when I switched back.
After deleting and recreating the second virtual desktop, I could no longer reproduce it consistently.
N1.label: N1 Spaces-dependent behavior established

symptoms_visible: On another affected Tauri 1.7 app, the duplicate menu icon appears in Dark mode but not in Light mode.
Changing from Dark to Light makes the duplicate disappear, and changing back to Dark does not immediately bring it back.
N2.label: N2 second affected deployment and theme behavior

symptoms_visible: The duplicate menu icon appeared again during App Store review even though my manifest declared Tauri 1.7.2 and tauri-runtime-wry 0.14.10.
N2_x.label: N2_x dependency update alone did not establish resolution

symptoms_visible: A user on another affected deployment can reproduce the extra icon around macOS Spaces, and switching Spaces makes it disappear.
N3.label: N3 independent Spaces reproduction before update

symptoms_visible: Another operator reports that updating to the stated Tauri dependencies and doing a clean build stopped the ghost icon on their affected deployment.
I have not retested the final build on my original mirrored-monitor setup.
N_terminal.label: terminal with relayed successful verification

question_patterns: Are multiple macOS Spaces or virtual desktops active when the extra icon appears?
Does the number of virtual desktops affect whether you can reproduce it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I had two virtual desktops defined. I couldn't reproduce it after removing one and leaving only a single desktop.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I only use one virtual desktop, and the icon appears consistently without an external monitor.
I have three virtual desktops rather than two, but the same behavior occurs.

question_patterns: What happens if you switch to another Space after the ghost icon appears?
Does changing virtual desktops affect the duplicate icon?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the ghost icon appears, switching to a different virtual desktop makes it disappear. It doesn't reappear when I switch back to the original desktop.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Switching Spaces has no effect; the duplicate remains until I quit the app.

question_patterns: Can you still reproduce it after removing and recreating the additional Space?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After deleting one virtual desktop and recreating it, I could no longer reproduce the issue even with two desktops. It seems like a Heisenbug.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c4-c5: the original reporter supplied the Spaces dependency and transient clearing behavior after maintainers engaged. These facts are therefore collected here rather than placed in the opening body.

question_patterns: Does this still occur in a current Tauri 1.7 app on another affected machine?
Which Tauri series is the affected app using?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I updated my app to the latest Tauri 1.7 version and still see the system menu double icon.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The issue stopped completely as soon as I updated from Tauri 1.5 to 1.7.

question_patterns: Does the macOS Light or Dark appearance affect the duplicate icon?
Can you compare the menu bar in both system appearance modes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my machine the double icon appears when macOS is set to Dark. In Light mode the icon is normal.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It appears identically in Light and Dark mode, and changing appearance never clears it.
It appears in Dark mode with a different wallpaper and menu bar tint.

question_patterns: What happens after changing the macOS appearance while the duplicate icon is visible?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Switching from Dark to Light makes the duplicate disappear. Switching back to Dark did not immediately bring it back.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The duplicate still clears after changing appearance, but it returns after restarting the app.

edges.comment: Second affected user c7-c8 is explicitly folded into the simulated user side. This is a separate deployment from the opening reporter's mirrored-monitor setup; its screenshots establish a related transient trigger and show that a general Tauri 1.7 update had not yet eliminated the issue.

solution.intent: Treat upgrading within the Tauri 1.7 series by itself as sufficient and assume the previously reported tray changes have resolved the duplicate icon.
solution.concrete_example: Update the Tauri 1.x dependencies and resubmit the same application without first confirming the resolved dependency graph or doing a clean rebuild.

edges.comment: Second affected user c13: the App Store rejection recurred after updating the app, with Cargo.toml declaring Tauri 1.7.2 and tauri-runtime-wry 0.14.10. Thus a generic claim that any 1.7-series update alone proves resolution was falsified.

question_patterns: Can another affected deployment reproduce the icon, and is it associated with macOS Spaces?
Does the duplicate still occur for users who switch between Spaces?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have a user who can reproduce the extra icon, and it seems related to macOS Spaces.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The user's duplicate icon is unrelated to Spaces and remains visible across every desktop and display state.

question_patterns: What happens on that deployment when the user switches Spaces?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When the user switches Spaces, the extra icon goes away.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Switching Spaces clears it, but it sometimes returns on a later launch.

edges.comment: Third affected deployment reported by adamplouff in c17 is folded explicitly. This is relayed evidence about that operator's user, not a new observation from the opening reporter and not proof that the original setup is fixed.

solution.intent: Use the corrected Tauri v1 tray implementation by updating to the stated 1.7.2-era dependencies, regenerating the resolved dependency state with a clean Cargo build, and then verify on the affected multi-Space or multi-display setup before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Use Tauri 1.7.2 with tauri-runtime-wry 0.14.10, remove the stale Cargo.lock used in the reported attempt if necessary, perform a clean Cargo build, and retest while using the Spaces or multi-monitor state that previously produced the ghost icon.
solution.inference_hint: The thread establishes only that maintainers' older reproduction stopped after the Tauri tray changes and that another affected operator reported success after the exact dependency update and clean build. It does not establish a lower-level AppKit mechanism, nor prove that deleting Cargo.lock itself was the causal fix.

edges.comment: Resolution evidence combines c15-c19 without pretending all messages describe one machine. A maintainer reported that the old reproduction was fixed by the Tauri changes; kurdin reported no current local reproduction after a clean build; adamplouff then reported that the exact update and clean-build guidance worked for a separate affected user. The opening reporter never retested, so terminal resolution remains relayed rather than personally verified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify this as the known Tauri macOS system-tray ghost-icon defect addressed by the corrected Tauri v1 tray changes; the thread does not establish a deeper AppKit mechanism.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected transient-state evidence: the duplicate is associated with mirrored or multiple displays and macOS Spaces, and switching Spaces or system appearance can clear it.
Must not claim that a generic update within the Tauri 1.7 series is sufficient; the duplicate was still observed after an earlier update in that series and even recurred during App Store review.

The final recommendation must use the stated Tauri 1.7.2-era dependencies, refresh the resolved dependency/build state with a clean Cargo build, and retest under the affected Spaces or display conditions.
Switching Spaces or toggling Light and Dark appearance may be described only as temporary symptom clearing, not as the underlying fix.

Must not declare the opening reporter's setup resolved solely because another operator reported success; request verification from the affected reporter on a build containing the corrected tray changes.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Tauri application developer who can provide a minimal Rust reproduction, dependency versions, App Store review evidence, and test updated builds.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and practical; volunteers new reproduction details as they emerge, acknowledges intermittent behavior, and offers to test proposed changes.
